To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the action potential duration of Purkinje fiber was prolonged by low calcium concentrations and shortened by high calcium concentrations.
the transmembrane potentials of Purkinje fibres are changed by alterations in the calcium concentration in the perfusion medium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of transmembrane potential of the Purkinje fiber and the effect of CaCl2 on it.
the study of the effects of variation in extracellular calcium concentration on the transmembrane potential of the Purkinje fiber.
the effects of changes in calcium concentration on action potentials of Purkinje fibres.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of calcium on the action potential are complex, and that the effects are dependent on the concentration of calcium and on the rate of stimulation.

an increase in the concentration of extracellular calcium increases the rate of depolarization and repolarization of the Purkinje fibers, while a decrease in the concentration of calcium has the opposite effect.
the effect of changes in the extracellular calcium concentration on the electrical activity of the heart is dependent on the calcium concentration and the stimulus rate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calcium concentration is an important determinant of the action potential of the cardiac cell and that the effect of calcium is not a simple one but depends on the concentration.
in 2X and 4X CaCl2 solutions the rate of the CaCl2-induced diastolic depolorization is increased, and that in 1/4 and 1/2 CaCl2 solutions, the repolarization of the action potential is delayed.

the action potential of the Purkinje fiber is sensitive to the calcium concentration in the perfusing solution, and that changes in calcium concentration may alter the transmembrane potential and the excitability of Purkinje tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calcium is a critical element in regulating heart function.
calcium can have a significant impact on the action potential and the transmembrane potential.
